transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Taking care of my mom on top of work has thrown my whole life off, and I feel like I’m not handling any of it the way I usually would. It's just gotten to be too much to juggle on my own, and I don't know how to get back on track.

Did these feelings start after your mother’s care needs increased, or have you been feeling this way more generally for at least several months even outside of that stress? Also, do you still enjoy things you usually like, or has interest in most things dropped off?

These feelings definitely started right after my mom's stroke and I took on her care about four months ago, rather than being a long-standing issue. And yes, I've stopped doing things I used to love; I’ve been bailing on my church activities and my classic-truck club because I'm just too overwhelmed and exhausted.

Aside from feeling overwhelmed by caregiving, have you been feeling down or hopeless most of the day nearly every day for at least two weeks? And have you also had changes in sleep, appetite, energy, concentration, or feelings of worthlessness?

I don't think it's a constant, hopeless depression, but I am definitely running on fumes and lying awake at night beating myself up. My concentration is also pretty shot because I'm constantly distracted thinking about my mom's meds, though my appetite is fine. It all really just comes down to the sheer exhaustion of trying to juggle her care and my job.

When you do get a break from caregiving or things with your mom feel more manageable, do your mood and energy improve noticeably? Or do the sadness, loss of interest, and self-criticism stay about the same even then?

To be honest, I haven't really had a true break lately to even know, since the demands are constant. But I fully expect that once my mom's situation stabilizes and she doesn't need this level of care, I'll be able to get back to my normal self and routine. I don't think this overwhelmed feeling is permanent; it's just tied directly to how intense everything is right now.

Over the past two weeks, have you felt sad or unable to enjoy almost anything most of the day nearly every day, even during brief moments when caregiving demands were lighter? Or do those feelings mainly come up when you’re dealing with your mom’s care and work stress?

These feelings aren't constant for no reason; they are directly tied to the overwhelming pressure of juggling my mom's care and my job. It's this stressful situation that triggers me to cry, snap at my coworkers, and skip out on things I love like church and my truck club. I really believe that once her situation stabilizes and the caregiving burden eases, I'll be able to get back to my normal, happier self.

final_diagnosis.reason: Symptoms began in direct temporal relation to an identifiable psychosocial stressor (mother’s stroke and caregiving burden) about four months ago and are characterized by distress and functional disruption tied to that stressor. The patient does not describe a pervasive, autonomous major depressive syndrome; symptoms are understood as stress-linked and expected to remit when the caregiving situation improves, supporting an adjustment disorder diagnosis.
